questions.lead_text: City planners increasingly rely on data to design walkable neighborhoods.
sentences: Sensors track pedestrian flow at major intersections throughout the day.
This information helps planners decide where to widen sidewalks.
Many residents also enjoy weekend farmers markets downtown.
It also reveals which crossings need longer signal times for safety.
Over time, this data-driven approach reduces accidents significantly.

questions.passage_lead: Every organization eventually faces a moment when old habits no longer fit new challenges.
questions.para_a: (A) Leaders who recognize this early can guide the transition before a crisis forces it.
questions.para_b: (B) Those who ignore the signals often find themselves reacting too late, under far worse conditions.
questions.para_c: (C) The difference between the two outcomes usually comes down to how honestly the team assesses its own blind spots.

questions.given_sentence: Yet not all delays are harmful; some allow better decisions to emerge.
questions.lead_text: Waiting is often treated as wasted time in modern culture.
rest_sentences: People are told to act quickly and decisively whenever possible.
A rushed choice under pressure can overlook important details.
Research on negotiation shows that patience frequently produces better terms for both sides.
This does not mean every decision benefits from delay, of course.
